item.title: Bufo-Real
item.description:
Scientific name: Bubo bubo

The horned owl is a relatively large species with a length of 30 to 37 cm, a wingspan of 22.8 to 29.4 cm and a weight of 320 to 546g.

They hunt at dusk. They feed on birds, large insects, lizards, birds, reptiles, small mammals such as rodents and bats (including vampire bats Desmodus rotundus), small vertebrates and snakes.

item.title: Charneco
item.description:
Scientific name: Cyanopica cyanus

This bird is native to the south of the Iberian Peninsula (Portugal and Spain) and also to China, Korea, Japan, northern Mongolia and southern Russia.

This particular distribution is due to the fragmentation of a continuous population that stretched from the Iberian Peninsula to the Far East around 1.2 million years ago. The split was due to climate change caused by the last Ice Age: the reduction in temperature was so marked that the populations of this species disappeared from Eastern Europe and the Middle East, with only the populations at the extremes of the Eurasian continent remaining. They found refuge there because the temperatures were more tolerable.

item.title: Garça-real
item.description:
Scientific name: Ardea cinerea

It is the most abundant and widespread heron in Europe. It has a length of around 95 cm, a wingspan of 185 cm and a weight of 1.6 to 2 kg. It can live for around 25 years.

It feeds mainly on fish, but does not disdain batrachians, reptiles, small mammals, insects or terrestrial and aquatic molluscs. It digests bones well, but regurgitates rodent hair in the form of balls.

item.title: Garça-real 2
item.description:
Scientific name: Ardea cinerea

The gray heron, also known as the great white egret, is a bird species from the order Pelecaniformes. It is very common and widespread in Eurasia and Africa.

There are four subspecies worldwide. In Central Europe, it is represented by the nominate form Ardea cinerea cinerea.

The grey heron reaches a body length of 90 to 98 centimetres and usually weighs between 1 and 2 kilograms.

The house sparrow is omnivorous and feeds on a variety of insects, worms and berries.

It is one of the most widespread species in the country. Its habitat is forests, pastures with hedges, urban parks and gardens, dense scrubland and also riparian galleries.

item.title: Papa-figos
item.description:
Scientific name: Oriolus oriolus

They grow to about 24 to 25 cm long and have a wingspan of 44 to 47 cm. They can live for ten years or longer and weigh between 65 and 67 grams.

They breed in deciduous forests and agricultural areas with deciduous trees in the vicinity of rivers and lakes, but also in large parks.

item.title: Pardal
item.description:
Scientific name: Passer domesticus

House sparrows are between 13 and 18 centimeters long, have a wingspan of 19 to 25 cm and weigh between 10 and 40 grams.

They live close to humans, both in cities and in the countryside, and feed on seeds, flowers, insects and food scraps left behind by humans.

They lay up to eight eggs, which are incubated by both parents, usually for 12 to 14 days.

item.title: Rola Turca
item.description:
Scientific name: Streptopelia decaocto

The Eurasian collared dove is one of the great colonizers in the bird world. Its original range was limited to temperate regions from south-eastern Europe to Japan. In the 20th century, however, this bird expanded its distribution throughout Europe. It even breeds in regions such as Scandinavia and north of the Arctic Circle. It arrived on the Iberian Peninsula in 1960 and in Portugal in 1974. Since then, it has spread and multiplied very rapidly.

item.title: Tordo
item.description:
Scientific name: Turdus philomelos

The song thrush is a medium-sized bird, 20-23 cm long, with a wingspan of 33-36 cm and a weight of 50-107 g.

In Portugal, it feeds mainly on olives, but also on invertebrates , especially earthworms and snails, smashing the shells by hitting them against a stone, berries and fruit. It is the most common of the various thrush species found on the Portuguese mainland and the species most frequently killed by hunters.
